title: myself/yourself/themselves etc.
subtitle: I hurt myself
summary: Use myself/yourself/himself etc. when the subject and the object are the same person, and use each other when two people do something to one another.

lesson.heading: Subject and object are the same
lesson.text: At a party Steve says *'Hi, I'm Steve.'* **Steve introduced himself** to the other guests. We use **myself/yourself/himself** etc. (reflexive pronouns) when the subject and the object of the verb are the same person.

examples.text: I don't want you to pay for me. I'll pay for **myself**.
Amy had a great holiday. She really enjoyed **herself**.
If you want more to eat, help **yourselves**.
examples.note: said to more than one person

lesson.note: Compare: Lisa introduced **me** to the other guests. / I introduced **myself** to the other guests.

lesson.heading: Verbs that do not take myself etc.
lesson.text: We do not use **myself/yourself** etc. after **feel, relax, concentrate** or **meet**. And we normally do not use them after **wash, shave** and **dress** either.
lesson.note: You can also say **get dressed**: He **got dressed** and went out.

lesson.heading: -selves or each other?

left.label: themselves
left.text: Each person does something to himself or herself.
examples: Kate and Joe stood in front of the mirror and looked at **themselves**.
If people work too hard, they can make **themselves** ill.

right.label: each other
right.text: The two people do something to one another.
examples: Kate looked at Joe, and Joe looked at Kate. They looked at **each other**.
How long have you and Ben known **each other**?
Sue and Alice don't like **each other**.

lesson.note: You can use **one another** instead of **each other**: Do they live near each other? or ... near one another?

lesson.heading: myself etc. for emphasis
lesson.text: We also use **myself/yourself** etc. to emphasise a word - to say *this person and not another person*. *'Who repaired your bike?'* *'I repaired it **myself**.'* = I repaired it, nobody else did.

examples.text: I'm not going to do your work for you. You can do it **yourself**.
Let's paint the house **ourselves**. It will be much cheaper.
The film **itself** wasn't very good, but I loved the music.
Lisa doesn't think so **herself**. or Lisa **herself** doesn't think so.

lesson.text: Ask yourself who does what: if the person doing the action and the person receiving it are the same, use -self/-selves; if two people do it to one another, use each other.

exercises.prompt: Amy had a great holiday. She really ___.
exercises.explanation: The subject (she) and the object are the same person, so we use the reflexive pronoun herself.

exercises.prompt: Ben fell down some steps, but fortunately he didn't ___.
exercises.explanation: Ben is the person who is hurt, so the object is himself.

exercises.prompt: It isn't Sue's fault. She really shouldn't ___.
exercises.explanation: Sue would be blaming Sue, so subject and object are the same: blame herself.

exercises.prompt: It's not my fault. You can't blame ___.
exercises.explanation: You and me are different people, so we use me, not myself.

exercises.statement: I climbed out of the swimming pool and dried myself with a towel.
exercises.explanation: Correct. I dried me, so the reflexive pronoun myself is right.

exercises.statement: I tried to study, but I couldn't concentrate myself.
exercises.explanation: I tried to study, but I couldn't concentrate. We do not use myself after concentrate.

exercises.prompt: Be careful! That pan is hot. Don't ___.
exercises.explanation: Said to one person, so the reflexive pronoun is yourself.

exercises.prompt: Which of these verbs normally take myself/yourself etc. when the subject and object are the same, and which never take them?
How long have you and Ben known ___?
exercises.explanation: You know Ben and Ben knows you, so we say each other (or one another).

exercises.prompt: Some people are selfish. They only think of ___.
exercises.explanation: Each selfish person thinks about that same person, not about one another: themselves.

exercises.prompt: You didn't buy this cake from a shop. Say who made it.
exercises.explanation: Here myself emphasises I - I made it, not a shop.

exercises.prompt: 'Who told you Laura was going away?' 'Laura ___.'
exercises.explanation: Herself emphasises Laura: Laura told me, nobody else did.
